Until recently, such concerns about South Korean decision-making would have been easily dismissed. In democracies, major national security decisions are typically made through consultation with civilian and military advisors, with cooler heads prevailing. South Korea, as a flourishing democracy, has long been perceived as a rational and responsible actor. If it were to acquire nuclear weapons, the assumption has been that it would do so purely to deter its erratic and dangerous nuclear-armed neighbor.
